sovereign_country.strategic_role: 西欧核心消费市场、高客单价品牌合规与本土清关

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Personal Wealth Analytics and Investment Tracking Cloud

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: France-United States Double Taxation Convention (as amended by 2009 Protocol)
France-United Kingdom Double Taxation Convention (1968, as amended)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Articles L561-1 to L561-54 and R561-1 to R561-60 of the French Monetary and Financial Code (Code monétaire et financier); Decree No. 2018-284 of 18 April 2018 transposing EU Directive 2015/849 (AMLD5) and EU Directive 2018/843 (AMLD6); Article L561-2-2 on the UBO register and Article R561-28 of the same Code; Commercial Code Articles L123-11-2 and R123-166 (registered office and UBO filing).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized copy of each shareholder/managing director's passport or national identity card
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the shareholder's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (if country is a 1961 Hague Conference signatory); otherwise consular legalization by the French Embassy

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation and certificate of good standing of any corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Official company register in the corporate shareholder's jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney granted to the French incorporation agent or domiciliary agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the shareholder's country
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization if the origin country is not a Hague signatory

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all beneficial owners, shareholders, managers, and directors against the French national (DG Trésor) asset-freeze list, the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, the UN Security Council Consolidated List, and the OFAC SDN List. PEP checks must be conducted under Article L561-5 of the Monetary and Financial Code, with enhanced due diligence applied to any person holding, or having held within the last 12 months, a high-ranking political office, and to family members or known associates. Documentary KYC by AML/CFT officers must be completed before incorporation filing; refusal to cooperate constitutes grounds for rejection of the SARL registration.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet Unique des Formalités Entreprises (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr) and the official RCS database (Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés) administered by INPI (Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle) via Infogreffe.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name of a SARL may be in French or any Latin-alphabet language; if non-Latin script is used, a standard transliteration into Latin characters (AFNOR NF ISO 7098 for Chinese) must be provided and the French spelling must be used in the articles and in all official filings. Names must not be contrary to French public policy, must not mislead the public as to the company's purpose or legal form, and must not be identical or phonetically indistinguishable from an existing RCS entry or a protected trademark.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the greffe (commercial court registry) rejects the name because of identity or similarity with an existing entry, the applicant may file an amended registration through the Guichet Unique within 15 days of the rejection notice. The applicant may also submit a written contestation before the President of the Commercial Court (Tribunal de Commerce) under summary jurisdiction (Article R123-96 Commercial Code), attaching the rejection notice and proof of prior trademark search. If the conflict arises from a prior trademark registered at INPI, the applicant may file an opposition with INPI within two months of the registration publication, or seek a coexistence agreement; otherwise the de novo refiling is recommended. Extensions of the 30-day clearance window are not automatic; a new search and revalidation must be conducted after expiry.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted for administrative domiciliation under Article L123-11-2 of the French Commercial Code, subject to a maximum continuous period of 5 years. The virtual office provider must be a registered domiciliation company (société de domiciliation) located in France and must be able to receive and forward official correspondence on a daily basis. For a low-risk fintech software application with no statutory financial license, the use of a virtual office is admissible, but the registered address must appear on the Kbis extract and be located within the territorial jurisdiction of the registration court.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low risk — estimated 7% probability of an unannounced physical on-site inspection per fiscal year, primarily triggered by an AML/CFT risk assessment, tax audit, or a third-party complaint. The domiciliation agent must be available for inspection and able to produce all statutory records, including UBO declarations and board minutes, within one hour.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Company name clearance and RCS/INPI search certificate (legal nature check)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory fee schedule for registry data retrieval and legal nature verification

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization and apostille/consular legalization of shareholder identity documents and power of attorney
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary public in shareholder's country of residence + competent foreign ministry or French consulate
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Notarial regulated tariff and government consular fee schedule

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Virtual office / domiciliation agreement (first year subscription)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark; fixed annual fee per French domiciliation industry standards

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Publication of legal notice (annonce légale) in an approved legal gazette (JAL)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Authorized legal announcements journal (Journal d'Annonces Légales)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff set by Decree No. 2023-776; cost dependent on number of legal lines

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Filing of incorporation dossier with the commercial court registry (greffe) via Guichet Unique
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce / INPI
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Fixed public tariff listed in French commercial registry fee schedule (frais de greffe)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Drafting of SARL articles of association and English translation, if applicable, by a licensed French legal advisor
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Law firm or legal tech provider admitted in France
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark / fixed professional service fee; not a statutorily fixed tariff

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/CFT KYC and UBO background checks on beneficial owners and directors (third-party database subscriptions and compliance officer time)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: AML compliance service provider or internal compliance officer
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark; flat fee per individual screened against PEP and sanctions lists

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce) Articles L.210-1 to L.210-11, L.223-1 to L.223-43, and R.223-1 et seq.; French Civil Code Articles 1832 et seq. for general company contract formation.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Commercial Court Registry) via the Guichet Unique operated by the Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Statuts of a Société à Responsabilité Limitée, filed as a certified incorporation dossier through the Guichet Unique for registration on the Registre National des Entreprises (RNE) and the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum statutory capital for a SARL; founders may set capital freely. Cash contributions must be fully paid up at subscription and deposited with a French bank or notary escrow. If in-kind contributions exceed EUR 30,000 or if no in-kind valuation exists, a statutory auditor (Commissaire aux Apports) must assess their value. Escrow release occurs upon successful RCS registration or upon official refusal/abandonment.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the subscribers, constituting the initial shareholders of the SARL, hereby adopt the draft Articles of Association. RESOLVED, that each shareholder acknowledges full subscription and payment of the cash contribution set opposite his/her name, and that the capital is held by the company subject to the escrow rules of Article L.223-7. RESOLVED, that the registered office be established at [Address], France, with jurisdiction of the Commercial Court of [Town]. RESOLVED, that [Full Name], domiciled at [Address], be appointed as Gérant (Manager) for an indefinite term, with full powers to operate the business and represent the company. RESOLVED, that the necessary formalities be completed and that this resolution be filed with the commercial registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of the Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Founding shareholders and legal counsel; statutory deed shall be signed before one or more notaries if a non-cash contribution of immovable property is involved, otherwise private deed.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare French-language statutes in duplicate, specify share capital divided into shares, limit the corporate object to the ISIC 6201 financial portfolio tracking software service, include the registered office address, manager identity, notice provisions, and dispute resolution clauses. Obtain shareholder signatures; have signatures authenticated if the company pursues real-estate-related or notarial filings.
required_dossiers: Identity documents of all subscribing shareholders
Bank certificate or notary receipt confirming cash capital deposit
Inventory of in-kind contributions and valuation report if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If documents are legally insufficient, counsel immediately files a supplementary instrument and re-executes the statutes to cure the defect before formal filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: An authorized legal announcement journal (Journal d'annonces légales) in the department where the registered office is located.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Publish a mandatory notice containing the company name, legal form, share capital, registered office, corporate object, manager name, and the intended RCS registration court. Certify a copy of the published issue or obtain the official announcement number.
required_dossiers: Company name reservation certificate or declaration
Final draft statutes with registered office and manager details
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the announcement omits required particulars, file a corrective announcement with the same journal and enclose both versions in the registration dossier.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log on to the portal, select 'société en cours de constitution', input all SARL constitutional data, upload the statutes and required annexes, pay the state filing fee by card or bank order, and submit. The portal transmits the dossier electronically to the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce.
required_dossiers: Identity documents of managers and shareholders
Declaration of non-conviction or sworn statement of the manager
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry raises a query, correct and re-submit the invalidated fields within 15 days through the Guichet Unique. Incomplete packages are automatically rejected; after the third unsuccessful attempt, a fresh dossier must be transmitted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration with the Commercial Court Registry (Greffe)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce of the registered office jurisdiction.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The Greffe verifies legal compliance, checks conflicts with existing company names, and registers the SARL on the Registre National des Entreprises and the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés. Upon success, the Kbis extract is issued.
required_dossiers: Accepted dossier from Guichet Unique (automatic transmission)
Envelope with original signatures of statutes and incorporation documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Seek the President of the Commercial Court's summary order (référé) if the registry refuses without legal cause, or file a new application after curing the objection.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP), URSSAF, and the chosen commercial bank.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Receive the Kbis extract, open a corporate bank account, obtain the SIRET and SIREN numbers, complete anti-money-laundering due diligence for designated persons, and apply for VAT registration if taxable turnover threshold is reached.
required_dossiers: Commitment to French data protection and GDPR compliance for financial portfolio data
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Notify DGFiP of any data mismatch; obtain a corrected Kbis extract from Infogreffe if any registered mention is inaccurate.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Direction Générale des Entreprises (DGE) – Services à l'économie numérique et aux activités de services.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable – the activity is a pure cloud-based fintech software service and requires no industrial or manufacturing permit; only an ERP software registration declaration may apply.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de la Transition Écologique – Inspection des Installations Classées (ICPE)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – ISIC 6201 software publishing does not constitute an installation classée under the French Environment Code; no EIA or ICPE authorization is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable as no industrial wastewater, VOC, or waste-emission process exists. The service company must comply with EU General Data Protection Regulation for electronic data processing and, where relevant, with energy reporting under the French Energy Efficiency Directive and the AGEC law for IT equipment waste.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification is not required for a class 5 ERP unless the leased premises exceed applicable thresholds; however, the company must conduct a fire safety inspection of all office facilities, obtain structural load clearance for any IT server racks or heavy equipment, and comply with French Labour Code workplace health clearance requirements (Articles R.4212 et seq.).

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction générale des Finances publiques (DGFiP); businesses use the professional area of impots.gouv.fr and deal with the competent Service des impôts des entreprises (SIE). Company formation and initial registration are filed through the Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises, operated by INPI; INSEE assigns the SIREN and SIRET identifiers.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a French SARL, file incorporation and registration formalities through the Guichet unique, including the registered office, activity, managers, beneficial owners, and required corporate documents. On registration in the Registre national des entreprises and, where applicable, the Registre du commerce et des sociétés, INSEE assigns a SIREN and establishment-level SIRET; the DGFiP communicates the tax account and applicable corporate tax arrangements. A French VAT number is generally issued by the competent SIE after VAT registration; it uses the FR prefix and the prescribed key followed by the SIREN. A foreign-established taxable person without a French establishment must register with the competent French non-resident tax service before carrying out transactions requiring French VAT compliance; a non-EU-established person generally appoints a French fiscal representative unless an applicable mutual-assistance arrangement provides an exception. EU-established persons generally do not require a fiscal representative. OSS may be used for eligible cross-border EU B2C supplies but does not replace domestic registration obligations where those independently arise.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A SARL is generally subject to French corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés, or IS). A qualifying SARL may elect temporary income-tax transparency under the small-business option, generally for up to five financial years and subject to statutory ownership, age, activity, and size conditions. A qualifying family-owned SARL conducting an eligible commercial, industrial, craft, or agricultural activity may elect the family-SARL partnership regime without that five-year limit, subject to continuing eligibility. These are statutory French tax elections, not US-style check-the-box elections; France has no general entity-classification election for a SARL. Hybrid mismatch rules may deny deductions or impose inclusions in relevant cross-border arrangements but do not constitute an entity-classification election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT; taxe sur la valeur ajoutée, or TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general turnover threshold applies to a non-established taxable person making French-taxable supplies: registration is generally required from the first such transaction. A France-established small business may qualify for the domestic VAT franchise under applicable turnover limits; the general services threshold is EUR 37,500, with a higher tolerance threshold of EUR 41,250 under the rules applicable from 2025, subject to statutory conditions and legislative changes. The franchise is not a general exemption from registration for non-established suppliers. For electronically supplied B2C services to consumers in other EU Member States, the EU-wide EUR 10,000 threshold may affect place-of-supply treatment for eligible suppliers; OSS can be used to report destination-country VAT.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France is introducing mandatory domestic B2B e-invoicing and transaction/payment e-reporting through approved platforms. From 1 September 2026, all in-scope businesses must be able to receive e-invoices; large and medium-sized businesses must issue them from that date, while SMEs and microbusinesses are generally required to issue them from 1 September 2027. Applicable B2C and cross-border transactions are generally subject to e-reporting rather than domestic B2B e-invoicing. The system is not a universal real-time pre-clearance or fiscal-stamping regime. Businesses must use the prescribed formats and transmission channels and comply with applicable platform and reporting requirements.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods dispatched or transported from France to a destination outside the EU may qualify for VAT exemption with the right to deduct input VAT, provided statutory export conditions are met and the supplier retains evidence that the goods left the EU. Intra-EU supplies are subject to separate exemption conditions, including customer VAT identification and transport evidence. Services are not automatically zero-rated as exports: B2B services are generally taxed where the business customer is established, often with customer-side reverse charge, while B2C electronically supplied services are generally taxed where the consumer resides under applicable place-of-supply rules. A French portfolio-tracking software subscription therefore requires transaction-specific place-of-supply and customer-status analysis; an export label alone does not establish a 0% rate.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: For goods exported outside the EU: export customs declaration and its Movement Reference Number (MRN), together with customs exit confirmation or equivalent official evidence of exit.
Transport evidence appropriate to the shipment, such as a bill of lading, air waybill, CMR, carrier confirmation, or other reliable proof connecting the goods to the export.
Commercial invoice, order, and delivery records supporting the identity of the supplier, customer, goods, destination, and transaction.

For services: contract, invoice, customer business-status and establishment evidence, and records supporting the applicable place-of-supply treatment. A customs export declaration and inward remittance certificate are not generally applicable requirements for services.
A foreign-exchange repatriation certificate is not a general French VAT zero-rating condition.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The supplier must substantiate the conditions for exemption and retain supporting records for the applicable statutory retention period. If export or other exemption conditions are not proven, the DGFiP may assess French VAT, late-payment interest, and penalties. Intentional omissions or inaccurate returns may attract increased penalties; fraud may trigger the most severe tax penalties and, where the statutory elements are met, criminal prosecution. Input VAT refunds may be denied or recovered where the underlying transactions do not support deduction. France imposes no general 180-day foreign-exchange repatriation deadline for claiming export VAT treatment.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (BdF) in coordination with the European Central Bank (ECB) and the Direction Générale du Trésor (French Treasury) for exchange-rate policy, foreign-exchange reporting, and balance-of-payments compilation.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France, as a euro-area member state, maintains full and unrestricted convertibility for both capital-account and current-account transactions under Articles 63-66 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union and the French Monetary and Financial Code. Profit remittances, dividends, interest, royalties, repayments of shareholder loans, and liquidation proceeds may be freely transferred to non-residents without prior authorization or quantitative restriction. Settlement may be executed in EUR or any freely convertible currency. The only frictions are statistical declaration obligations for cross-border transactions and anti-money-laundering documentation requirements imposed by the credit institution.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France imposes no export-proceeds surrender requirement. There is no statutory timeline for repatriation and no mandatory conversion ratio for export receipts. Export proceeds in foreign currency may be retained, held on account, or converted freely. For balance-of-payments statistics, resident entities must report cross-border payments to the Banque de France regardless of currency, generally through their bank's periodic reporting framework; however, the reporting obligation does not restrict conversion or liquidity management.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium with legal constraints. Authorized or passported Electronic Money Institutions / Payment Institutions under PSD2 may provide payment accounts with French or European IBANs, cross-currency settlement, and SEPA/SWIFT routing, but they are not licensed credit institutions under French law. They cannot offer deposit-taking, interest-bearing current accounts, or capital escrow services in a manner equivalent to a full bank. For a France SARL requiring capital injection escrow and operational disbursements, a bank-licensed account is preferred; an EU-licensed EMI is viable only as a supplementary operating rail and must disclose that funds are not covered by the French deposit guarantee scheme (FGDR).
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Under French AML/FT rules and ACPR supervisory practice, a physical or video-verified interview of the legal representative (gérant), at least one director, the beneficial owner, and the accountants or in-house finance officers is generally required before account opening. Remote onboarding may be accepted by some banks using regulated eIDAS-qualified electronic identification, digital identity verification, and certified KYC package transfer (KYC file sharing), but the final decision is at the bank's discretion. For high-volume or cross-border treasury arrangements, French banks commonly require one in-person meeting at the corporate banking desk or an arranged appointment with the foreign entity's local counsel.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inconsistency between stated ISIC 6201 software activity and transaction flows involving large shareholder capital injections or high-frequency payment-card settlements.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed corporate presentation, audited or internally certified financial statements, software platform demonstration, roadmap and product documentation, executed client agreements and subscription contracts, revenue recognition policy, and board minutes confirming the capital injection and treasury purpose.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial owner or corporate shareholder resident in a higher-risk or sanctioned jurisdiction.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Structured ownership chart from the SARL to each ultimate individual, passport copies, proof of address, professional and institutional references, source-of-wealth documentation, bank references from the shareholder's home bank, and a notarized certification of no exposure to OFAC/EU-restrictive measures.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of virtual assets, cryptocurrency, or non-bank payment intermediaries for capital subscription or customer intakes.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Blockchain analytics report, transaction traces, custody statements, exchange KYC/AML certificates, and documented explanation of the business reason for using each virtual-asset corridor, together with internal treasury policy prohibiting anonymous payments.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume outbound payments to entities in jurisdictions inconsistent with the French entity's corporate purpose.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Invoices, technology licensing or software-as-a-service agreements, transfer-pricing file, proof of economic substance (employees, office lease, payroll, procurement contracts), and a counterparty KYC questionnaire for every material beneficiary.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual frequency or size of same-day intra-group movements between the French SARL treasury account and affiliated holding companies.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Cash-pooling agreement, intercompany loan documentation, central treasury policy, board resolutions, regulatory reporting records under Banque de France balance-of-payments filings, and tax-neutral rationale memorandum to demonstrate arm's length terms.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Non-resident shareholders should route equity or shareholder-loan proceeds via SWIFT MT103 (customer credit transfer) from the remitting bank to the French SARL's EUR account. The underlying wire must reference a clear corporate action (e.g., 'Contribution en compte-courant d'associé' or 'Incorporation capital contribution'), and the French bank will require the executed shareholder resolution, articles of association, Crowe or notarial deed if applicable, beneficial-owner declarations, and source-of-funds evidence. For non-EEA inbound wires in foreign currency, settlement conversion to EUR is executed at market rate plus bank margin; the French bank reports the transaction for balance-of-payments statistics. All inbound remittances must emanate from the bank account of the qualified shareholder or lender; third-party financing through unlicensed money transmitters is not accepted.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade-related disbursements for software licensing, SaaS subscriptions, intercompany royalties, IT procurement, and consulting services are executed through SEPA Credit Transfer for EEA beneficiaries, SWIFT MT103 for non-EEA beneficiaries, and Commercial Letters of Credit (UCP600) where payment is conditional on documentary compliance. The French SARL treasury should maintain separate clearing rails: (i) SEPA direct debits and SEPA credit transfers for EU distribution partners and payroll; (ii) SWIFT MT103 with structured purpose codes (often referencing the EU BOP component type) for Asian and North American counterparties; and (iii) documentary collection or commercial LC for large-scale licensing or reseller transactions. Compliance files for each disbursement must include invoices, contracts, tax certificates, pre-validation of sanctions/embargo lists, and balance-of-payments declarations as required by the Banque de France.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX forward contracts denominated in EUR against USD, GBP, CHF, and primary Asian currencies, executed exclusively with licensed credit institutions

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for currencies with restricted convertibility, provided that underlying commercial exposure is documented and the French bank has designated a qualified offshore NDF desk
Cross-currency swaps (FX swaps and currency swaps) for long-term funding alignment between EUR shareholder loans and USD-denominated operating revenue
Currency options used on a documentary basis for treasury risk management only, subject to the bank's internal ISDA/CSA arrangements and unilateral French entity authorization

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Approval of annual accounts and discharge of the manager (Décision des associés - Assemblée Générale Ordinaire Annuelle)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: No regulator filing; records in the company's Minute Book (Registre des procès-verbaux des assemblées)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after fiscal year-end (e.g., by 30 June for a 31 December financial year; court prorogation possible)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to convoke or exercise the meeting: any associate may request the Commercial Court to order the holding of the meeting; legal costs and damages may be awarded.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Filing of annual financial statements (Dépôt des comptes annuels - bilan, compte de résultat et annexe) with the RCS
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) via the INPI Guichet Unique
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 1 month after shareholder approval and no later than 7 months after close (e.g., 31 July for 31 December year-end); court extension possible
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Manager is subject to a fine of up to €1,500; repeated failure can lead to formal notice and strike-off from the RCS; third-party liability risk.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax and results declaration (Liasse fiscale - n°2065 et annexes)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direction générale des Finances publiques (DGFiP), e-filing portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Calendar-year SARL: by 3 May after the accounting period (adjusted to the next business day); non-calendar year: within 3 months of fiscal close
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing: 10% penalty on unpaid tax; deliberate concealment: 40%; active concealment/repeat: 80%; late-payment interest at 0.20% per month.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: UBO declaration update (Déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs) — filed only on ownership changes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: RCS via the INPI Guichet Unique (attached to company file)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days of any change in beneficial ownership; no annual filing if data unchanged
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal penalties for the manager: up to 6 months imprisonment and €15,000 fine; the legal entity is fined up to €75,000.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory audit (commissaire aux comptes) is mandatory for a SARL if, at the end of the financial year, it exceeds two of the following thresholds: total balance sheet €4,000,000; net turnover excl. tax €8,000,000; average permanent employees 50. An audit may also be required by minority shareholders holding at least 1/10 of share capital or by court order.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP — ANC Regulation (Plan Comptable Général) for individual statutory accounts; IFRS only permitted for consolidated accounts; micro-entities may file simplified formats.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: France imposes no separate annual UBO confirmation statement; the RCS beneficial-owner file is a living record updated within 30 days of any change in ownership. The annual secretarial audit should verify that the RCS-stored UBO details match the register of members and any new declarations.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Registre des associés / registre des mouvements de titres)
Register of Shareholders' Meetings and Manager Decisions (Registre des délibérations et décisions)
Minute Book (Feuilles de présence and procès-verbaux of general meetings)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: $250 – $1,200 per year for commercial domiciliation in France; own premises may be free
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: $8,000 – $20,000 per year for a standard small/mid-size SARL statutory audit

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Standard IS rate 25%; reduced 15% on first €42,500 of profit for companies satisfying SME conditions (turnover below €10,000,000 and paid-in capital requirements); research tax credit (CIR) at 30% on eligible R&D expenditure up to €100,000,000; innovation tax credit (CII) at 20% for eligible SMEs; unlimited tax-loss carryforward with an annual usage cap of €1,000,000 plus 50% of taxable profit exceeding that amount.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulaire n° 2065-SD (CERFA 11274) with 2050-series annexes; mandatory electronic filing via 'Espace Professionnel' on impots.gouv.fr or through an approved EDI-TVA/EDI-IS transmitting software.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a fiscal year ending 31 December: second working day following 1 May. For an off-calendar fiscal year-end: within three months of the fiscal-year closing date.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company identification: legal name, legal form, SIREN, SIRET, APE/NAF code, registered office, and fiscal residence status.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The French SARL must use its French registration details; if the entity is treated as tax-transparent for French purposes, non-resident partners must attach a statement under Article 209B CGI regarding the French PE or deemed establishment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Financial statement summary: gross turnover, operating income, pre-tax accounting profit or loss, and total balance sheet.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report the full French statutory accounts of the SARL; attach a transfer-pricing adjustment schedule and any profit-attribution computation for French permanent-establishment purposes.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable result: determination of taxable income, deduction of prior-year losses, and calculation of deficit carryforward usage.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach a loss carryforward schedule proving the origin and use of deficits; losses of non-resident shareholders are not deductible unless a treaty PE in France exists and the loss is attributable to that PE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax computation: gross IS at 25% or reduced 15%, foreign tax credits, research tax credits, and advance payments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim treaty foreign-tax credits only where the underlying tax is recoverable and supported by a valid foreign tax credit certificate; include the credit annexes in the 2065-SD package.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of transactions with non-resident related parties, including fees, interest, royalties, and transfer-pricing documentation annexes (2257-SD) when thresholds are met.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident controlling shareholders must ensure the French entity reports all intragroup flows under LPF Articles L.13 AA and AB; keep the Local File and Master File ready for inspection.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing attracts a 10% automatic surcharge on the gross tax assessment; failure to file after a 30-day formal notice increases the surcharge to 40%; fraud or abusive behavior raises it to 80%. Late payment carries monthly interest at 0.20%. Non-electronic filing may incur an additional per-document penalty. Persistent non-compliance leads to ex officio assessment and criminal tax proceedings.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% on gross dividends paid by a French-resident SARL to non-resident corporate shareholders (CGI Art. 119 bis, 2°); 12.8% for non-resident individuals plus applicable social levies; treaty rates may reduce the rate to 0%, 5%, or 15% depending on the jurisdiction and shareholding level.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To apply a treaty-reduced rate at source, the non-resident shareholder must submit to the French paying entity before the distribution: (i) a valid tax residence certificate (TRC) issued by the shareholder's tax authorities, using form 5053 or an equivalent OECD-pattern certificate, and (ii) a beneficial ownership statement confirming the shareholder has the economic entitlement to the dividend. If excess withholding is applied, the shareholder must file a refund claim with the French non-resident tax service (DINR) within the applicable limitation period, generally by 31 December of the second calendar year following receipt of the dividend.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory withholding of 33.33% on patent and industrial-property royalties; treaty rates are commonly reduced to 0–10%. Interest: no general French domestic withholding tax on ordinary cross-border commercial or bank loan interest; treaty rates are generally 0%; payments to non-cooperative states are subject to a 75% levy under CGI Art. 238 A.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: France requires transfer-pricing documentation when the French entity's annual turnover or total assets exceed EUR 400,000,000 (LPF Art. L.13 AA). Group-wide Country-by-Country Reporting and Master File obligations arise when consolidated group revenue exceeds EUR 750,000,000. Entities below the thresholds must still maintain reliable functional, risk, and controlled-transaction records for tax audits.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France does not apply a Caribbean-style Economic Substance Regulation. Instead, anti-abuse doctrine operates through Article L.64 LPF (abus de droit), Article 155-A CGI, Article 119 bis CGI targeting interposed companies, and the Principal Purpose Test under double tax treaties. A French SARL without employees, premises, decision-making substance, or real risk-bearing activity is vulnerable to reclassification as a mere conduit, denial of treaty benefits, and reassessment of profit to the ultimate beneficiary.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion / Fraudulent Corporate Income Tax Reporting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willful omission of French taxable profits, deliberate non-filing of Form 2065-SD, suppression of turnover, use of fictitious invoices, or concealment of taxable transactions while maintaining an active French SARL.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative penalties up to 80% of evaded tax for fraudulent or abusive conduct, plus 0.20% monthly late-payment interest. Criminal conviction under CGI Art. 1741 carries up to €75,000 fine and 5 years imprisonment for simple tax fraud, and up to €1,000,000 fine and 10 years imprisonment for aggravated fraud; legal persons may be subject to multiplied fines, dissolution, and a business-activity ban.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable through veil-piercing and the action en comblement du passif; criminal personal fines and imprisonment may be imposed; courts may issue management bans, asset seizure, and travel restrictions during criminal proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the French SARL as a pure conduit with no office, staff, operational substance, or decision-making functions solely to obtain treaty benefits, shield ownership, or artificially reduce French taxation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment under Article L.64 LPF with an 80% penalty where abuse is committed in bad faith (40% otherwise); denial of treaty benefits; additional penalties for false declarations. The tax administration may also apply the general anti-abuse rules of EU ATAD and impose fines for non-declaration of beneficial ownership.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The court may disregard separate legal personality, hold directors jointly liable for recomputed tax and penalties, order personal restitution, and impose management bans of up to five years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Money Laundering / AML-KYC Failures in Fintech Portfolio Tracking
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating an investment-tracking application that conceals beneficial ownership, facilitates undisclosed assets, processes proceeds of tax fraud, fails to make suspicious transaction reports (déclaration de soupçon) to Tracfin, or omits beneficial-ownership registration in the RBE.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: ACPR administrative fines up to €5,000,000 or 10% of annual turnover for AML violations; criminal money-laundering sanctions up to 5 years imprisonment and €375,000 fine for individuals, with corporate fines multiplied to €1,875,000; confiscation of illicit assets and publication of sanctions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face criminal liability for complicity or intentional AML violations, personal asset confiscation, a ban on managing financial or commercial businesses, and travel bans pending criminal proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Booking non-arm's-length management fees, excessive software licence royalties, or unjustified portfolio-analytics charges to a foreign shareholder, leaving the French SARL with minimal profitability and no economic substance to support such payments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Ex officio reassessment of French taxable income under Article 57 CGI; application of a 40% deliberate misreporting penalty and late-payment interest; non-production of transfer-pricing documentation or forms 2257-SD may trigger mandatory administrative fines and evidentiary burdens against the taxpayer.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be sued for faute de gestion and ordered to restore shortfalls in corporate assets; if manipulation is linked to intentional tax evasion, personal criminal liability follows, including imprisonment and disqualification from corporate management.
